about.title: Los Gatos Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Los Gatos draws visitors and residents alike to its shops, restaurants, and hillside walkways, but uneven pavement, wet floors, poor lighting, or neglected stairways can turn an ordinary outing into an injury. Under California law, a property owner or business isn't automatically responsible just because someone got hurt on their premises — the injured person generally has to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why early documentation matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and incident reports filed with the business. Surveillance footage from stores along Los Gatos Boulevard or nearby shopping centers is often overwritten within days or weeks, so time is a factor. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect injured people with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property, the hazard, and the notice question at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Los Gatos

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises law hinges on notice — an attorney can help gather records, prior complaints, or maintenance logs showing the hazard existed long enough that it should have been addressed.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many Los Gatos businesses recycle their camera footage quickly; acting fast can mean the difference between having video evidence of the hazard and having none at all.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, you may still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Los Gatos?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If the fall happened on public property, such as a Town of Los Gatos sidewalk or building, the deadline is much shorter and requires a government claim first. Because of this, it's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible after the incident.

items.question: Do I need proof the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, in most cases California law requires showing the owner had actual or constructive notice of the dangerous condition and failed to address it within a reasonable time. Evidence like maintenance schedules, prior complaints, or how long a spill or hazard was visible can support this. An attorney can help identify and preserve this kind of evidence.

items.question: I fell at a store off Blossom Hill Road — will my own footwear or distraction hurt my claim?
items.answer: It might factor in, since California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation could be reduced by any percentage you're found responsible. But you can still recover even if you're partly at fault. An independent attorney can help assess how these facts might play out in your specific case.
